title: Understanding the Hierarchical Structure and Functional Landscape of the Model Context Protocol Ecosystem

paragraphs.en: AI agents increasingly rely on tools exposed through the Model Context Protocol (MCP) to complete user tasks. Hundreds of thousands of MCP servers are listed across marketplaces, yet they are organized only by coarse, marketplace-specific server categories. This makes it difficult for agents and users to identify tools for a given operation, find functional alternatives, and assess how those alternatives differ. We present MCPacific , the largest tool-level, cross-marketplace map of the MCP ecosystem. MCPacific collects 368,754 MCP server listings corresponding to 124,267 unique servers across 17 marketplaces, statically extracts 1,328,233 tool specifications from these servers in seven languages, and organizes them into a hierarchical functional taxonomy of 58,915 capabilities. We construct the taxonomy through an iterative LLM-driven design–test–refine process and map the full corpus to it using calibrated embedding routing. Our study reveals that MCP extends well beyond developer tooling, with 85% of tools serving other domains. Functional alternatives are widespread but unevenly distributed: 98.5% of tools have at least one alternative, yet nearly a quarter of capabilities are supported by only one tool. Functionally comparable tools also differ in security alerts, code complexity, and project maintenance, with complexity differing by more than 2.5 × \times in 41% of comparable tool pairs. Finally, presenting candidate tools through the taxonomy rather than a flat list improves task completion rate across all four evaluated models, with gains of up to 12 percentage points in Pass@0.75 for crowded candidate sets.

paragraphs.en: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly act on the world through external tools: they search the web, query databases, edit files, and operate software services ( Schick et al., 2023 ; Yao et al., 2022 ) . The Model Context Protocol (MCP) ( Anthropic, 2024 ) has quickly become a widely adopted standard for exposing such tools: an MCP server publishes a set of tools, each with a name, a natural-language description, and an input schema, and any MCP-compatible agent can discover and invoke them ( Model Context Protocol, 2026c ) . Within two years, this standard has produced an open ecosystem of more than 100,000 independently developed servers, advertised across many marketplaces.
paragraphs.zh: 大型语言模型（LLM）智能体正越来越多地通过外部工具对世界采取行动：它们可以搜索网络、查询数据库、编辑文件以及操作软件服务（Schick 等人，2023；Yao 等人，2022）。 模型上下文协议（MCP）（Anthropic，2024）已迅速成为暴露此类工具的广泛采用标准：一个 MCP 服务器会发布一组工具，每个工具都包含名称、自然语言描述和输入模式，任何兼容 MCP 的智能体都可以发现并调用这些工具（Model Context Protocol，2026c）。 在两年内，这一标准已经催生了一个开放生态系统，其中包含了超过 10 万个独立开发的服务器，并在多个市场平台上进行推广。

paragraphs.en: This openness turns tool use into a search problem. Before an agent can call a tool, it must find one that provides the needed capability; and when that tool is unavailable, deprecated, or insecure, it must find another that does the same job. Consider an agent tasked with sending an email through Gmail. In our taxonomy, 18 tools from different MCP servers provide this same capability, such as send_gmail_message , send_via_gmail , gmail_send , and gmail_send_email . The corresponding repositories range from 0 to 1,015 stars and were last updated between 15 and 480 days before collection. They are maintained by either organizations (e.g., Cloudgentic AI) or individual developers and implemented in diverse languages, including Python, Go, TypeScript, and C#. Despite relying on different providers and input schemas, they perform the same core function and may serve as alternatives. However, such relationships are not visible in existing marketplaces, which organize servers under coarse, marketplace-specific services, such as Communication and Workplace & Productivity, rather than indexing the capabilities of individual tools which are often documented only in source code. As a result, neither agents nor users can answer basic questions: Which capabilities does the ecosystem offer? Which tools can substitute for one another? And how do such alternatives differ?
paragraphs.zh: 这种开放性将工具使用转化为一个搜索问题。 在智能体调用某个工具之前，它必须找到一个能提供所需功能的工具；而当该工具不可用、已弃用或不安全时，它必须找到另一个能完成相同任务的工具。 假设有一个智能体的任务是使用 Gmail 发送电子邮件。 在我们的分类体系中，来自不同 MCP 服务器的 18 个工具提供了这一相同功能，例如 send_gmail_message、send_via_gmail、gmail_send 和 gmail_send_email。 这些工具对应的仓库获得的星星数从 0 到 1,015 不等，且在上次收集数据前 15 至 480 天内进行了最后更新。 它们由组织（例如 Cloudgentic AI）或个人开发者维护，并使用多种语言实现，包括 Python、Go、TypeScript 和 C#。 尽管这些工具依赖不同的提供商和输入模式，但它们执行着相同的核心功能，并可能互为替代方案。 然而，现有市场平台并未展示这类关系：它们将服务器按粗略且特定的服务类别进行组织，例如“通信”和“工作场所与生产力”，而不是对单个工具的功能进行索引，而这些功能通常仅在源代码中有文档说明。 因此，无论是智能体还是用户都无法回答一些基本问题：这个生态系统提供了哪些功能？ 哪些工具可以相互替代？ 这些替代方案之间又存在哪些差异？

paragraphs.en: Existing work does not answer these questions. Agent benchmarks ( Wang et al., 2026b ; Luo et al., 2025 ; Bandi et al., 2026 ; Mo et al., 2026 ) evaluate tool use within a limited set of curated servers, while tool-retrieval studies ( Qin et al., 2024 ; Fei et al., 2025 ; Wang et al., 2026a ) rank tools within fixed collections containing at most 177,436 tools, roughly 13% of the tools we extract, and organize them only into high-level task domains rather than tool-level functional categories. Ecosystem studies ( Guo et al., 2025 ; Lin et al., 2025 ; Chen et al., 2026 ; Toeppe et al., 2026 ; Hou et al., 2026 ) characterize servers through marketplace metadata, deployment properties, or security analyses, but remain largely at the server level, even though a single server may bundle dozens of tools that perform distinct operations. What is missing is a tool-level, functional view of the ecosystem: one that tells which operations exist and groups tools that perform the same operation, regardless of which server or marketplace lists them.

paragraphs.en: Building such a view poses three challenges. (C1) Fragmented sources. Servers are listed across heterogeneous marketplaces with different interfaces, duplicate entries, and inconsistent metadata. (C2) Hidden tools. Marketplaces rarely list the tools a server exposes; recovering them requires analyzing source code written in many languages, SDKs, and registration styles. (C3) No functional organization. Grouping more than a million tools by what they do requires categories that are fine-grained enough to separate operations, consistent across domains, and tested against real tools, at a cost that scales. We address these challenges with MCPacific , a tool-level, cross-marketplace map of the MCP ecosystem (Figure 1 ). MCPacific collects 368,754 listings from 17 marketplaces and resolves them to 124,267 unique source-available projects (C1). It then statically analyzes their source code with 30 language-specific recognition patterns, extracting 1,328,233 tool specifications from 110,482 projects in seven languages (C2), 7.5 × \times more tools than the largest prior collection ( Stein, 2026 ) . Finally, it organizes the tools into a hierarchical functional taxonomy of 58,915 leaf capabilities (C3). Inspired by recent work on software taxonomies ( Lu et al., 2026 ) , we build the taxonomy top-down: at each node, an LLM designs categories from sampled tools, tests them on a separate pilot sample, and refines them until they cover the tools with clear boundaries. We then map the full corpus with calibrated embedding routing and resolve the remaining tools through human review. Each leaf groups functionally comparable tools, i.e., tools that perform the same operation on the same kind of resource, even if they differ in provider, schema, or implementation. An evaluation on a uniform sample shows that 90.19% of eligible tools reach a leaf, 87.00% are assigned to the correct leaf, and 85.00% of same-leaf pairs are functionally comparable.
paragraphs.zh: 构建这样的视图存在三个挑战。（C1）来源碎片化。 服务器分散在具有不同接口、重复条目和不一致元数据的异构市场中。（C2）工具隐藏性。 市场很少列出服务器提供的工具；要恢复这些工具，需要分析用多种语言编写的源代码、SDK 和注册方式。 （C3）缺乏功能组织。 要将超过一百万个工具按功能分组，需要足够精细以区分不同操作、跨领域一致且经过真实工具验证的分类体系，同时成本还需具备可扩展性。 我们通过 MCPacific 应对这些挑战，这是一个面向工具层面、覆盖多个市场的 MCP 生态系统图谱（图 1）。 MCPacific 从 17 个市场收集了 368,754 条记录，并将其解析为 124,267 个独特的开源项目。（C1） 接着，它使用 30 种语言特定的识别模式对这些项目的源代码进行静态分析，从 110,482 个七种语言的项目中提取出 1,328,233 个工具规范。（C2）这一数量比此前最大的工具集合（Stein, 2026）多 7.5 倍。 最后，它将这些工具组织成一个包含 58,915 个叶级能力的分层功能分类体系。（C3） 受近期软件分类体系研究（Lu et al., 2026）的启发，我们采用自上而下的方式构建该分类体系：在每个节点，大型语言模型会根据抽样工具设计分类，在独立的试点样本中测试这些分类，并持续优化，直到它们能清晰覆盖所有工具且边界明确。 随后，我们通过校准后的嵌入路由对完整语料进行映射，并通过人工审核解决剩余工具的归属问题。 每个叶节点都汇集了功能上可比较的工具，即那些对同类型资源执行相同操作的工具，即使它们的提供商、模式或实现方式不同。 在统一样本上的评估显示：90.19% 的合格工具被归入某个叶节点，87.00% 被正确分配到对应的叶节点，且同一叶节点内的工具对中有 85.00% 是功能可比较的。

sents.zh: （C3）缺乏功能组织。

sents.en: Grouping more than a million tools by what they do requires categories that are fine-grained enough to separate operations, consistent across domains, and tested against real tools, at a cost that scales.
sents.zh: 要将超过一百万个工具按功能分组，需要足够精细以区分不同操作、跨领域一致且经过真实工具验证的分类体系，同时成本还需具备可扩展性。

sents.en: We address these challenges with MCPacific , a tool-level, cross-marketplace map of the MCP ecosystem (Figure 1 ).
sents.zh: 我们通过 MCPacific 应对这些挑战，这是一个面向工具层面、覆盖多个市场的 MCP 生态系统图谱（图 1）。

sents.en: MCPacific collects 368,754 listings from 17 marketplaces and resolves them to 124,267 unique source-available projects (C1).
sents.zh: MCPacific 从 17 个市场收集了 368,754 条记录，并将其解析为 124,267 个独特的开源项目。（C1）

sents.en: It then statically analyzes their source code with 30 language-specific recognition patterns, extracting 1,328,233 tool specifications from 110,482 projects in seven languages (C2), 7.5 × \times more tools than the largest prior collection ( Stein, 2026 ) .
sents.zh: 接着，它使用 30 种语言特定的识别模式对这些项目的源代码进行静态分析，从 110,482 个七种语言的项目中提取出 1,328,233 个工具规范。（C2）这一数量比此前最大的工具集合（Stein, 2026）多 7.5 倍。

sents.en: Finally, it organizes the tools into a hierarchical functional taxonomy of 58,915 leaf capabilities (C3).
sents.zh: 最后，它将这些工具组织成一个包含 58,915 个叶级能力的分层功能分类体系。（C3）

sents.en: Inspired by recent work on software taxonomies ( Lu et al., 2026 ) , we build the taxonomy top-down: at each node, an LLM designs categories from sampled tools, tests them on a separate pilot sample, and refines them until they cover the tools with clear boundaries.
sents.zh: 受近期软件分类体系研究（Lu et al., 2026）的启发，我们采用自上而下的方式构建该分类体系：在每个节点，大型语言模型会根据抽样工具设计分类，在独立的试点样本中测试这些分类，并持续优化，直到它们能清晰覆盖所有工具且边界明确。

sents.en: We then map the full corpus with calibrated embedding routing and resolve the remaining tools through human review.
sents.zh: 随后，我们通过校准后的嵌入路由对完整语料进行映射，并通过人工审核解决剩余工具的归属问题。

sents.en: Each leaf groups functionally comparable tools, i.e., tools that perform the same operation on the same kind of resource, even if they differ in provider, schema, or implementation.
sents.zh: 每个叶节点都汇集了功能上可比较的工具，即那些对同类型资源执行相同操作的工具，即使它们的提供商、模式或实现方式不同。

sents.en: An evaluation on a uniform sample shows that 90.19% of eligible tools reach a leaf, 87.00% are assigned to the correct leaf, and 85.00% of same-leaf pairs are functionally comparable.
sents.zh: 在统一样本上的评估显示：90.19% 的合格工具被归入某个叶节点，87.00% 被正确分配到对应的叶节点，且同一叶节点内的工具对中有 85.00% 是功能可比较的。

paragraphs.en: Using MCPacific as a measurement instrument, we conduct the largest empirical study of MCP tool functionality to date, organized around four research questions and their key findings:
paragraphs.zh: 我们将 MCPacific 用作测量工具，开展了迄今为止规模最大的 MCP 工具功能实证研究。该研究围绕四个研究问题及其关键发现展开：

paragraphs.en: RQ1 (Functional landscape): “Which capabilities does the ecosystem offer, and how are tools distributed across them?” Our study shows that 85% of tools serve domains beyond software development, including finance, media, and healthcare. At the same time, large domains fragment into thousands of narrow capabilities that coarse marketplace categories cannot distinguish.
paragraphs.zh: RQ1（功能全景）：“该生态系统提供了哪些能力，以及工具在这些能力之间是如何分布的？”我们的研究表明，85% 的工具服务于软件开发以外的领域，包括金融、媒体和医疗保健。 与此同时，大型领域会细分为数千个狭窄的能力，而这些能力是粗略的市场类别无法区分的。

sents.en: RQ1 (Functional landscape): “Which capabilities does the ecosystem offer, and how are tools distributed across them?” Our study shows that 85% of tools serve domains beyond software development, including finance, media, and healthcare.
sents.zh: RQ1（功能全景）：“该生态系统提供了哪些能力，以及工具在这些能力之间是如何分布的？”我们的研究表明，85% 的工具服务于软件开发以外的领域，包括金融、媒体和医疗保健。

sents.en: At the same time, large domains fragment into thousands of narrow capabilities that coarse marketplace categories cannot distinguish.
sents.zh: 与此同时，大型领域会细分为数千个狭窄的能力，而这些能力是粗略的市场类别无法区分的。

paragraphs.en: RQ2 (Functional comparability): “How often do tools have functionally comparable alternatives, and which capabilities lack them?” We find that functionally comparable alternatives are widespread but unevenly distributed: 98.5% of tools have at least one alternative and 74.1% have at least 20, yet nearly one quarter of capabilities are represented by only a single tool.
paragraphs.zh: RQ2（功能可比性）：“工具在多大程度上存在功能上可比的替代方案？哪些能力缺乏这样的替代方案？”我们发现，功能上可比的替代方案普遍存在，但分布并不均衡：98.5% 的工具至少有一个替代方案，74.1% 的工具至少有 20 个替代方案，但近四分之一的能力仅由单一工具所代表。

paragraphs.en: RQ3 (Alternative heterogeneity): “How do functionally comparable tools differ in security-relevant properties, code complexity, and project characteristics?” We find that comparable tools can differ substantially: security alerts often concentrate in only a subset of alternatives, cyclomatic complexity differs by more than 2.5 × \times for 41% of tool pairs, and in 60% of the capabilities we examine, some candidate projects are actively maintained while others are not.
paragraphs.zh: RQ3（替代方案异质性）：“功能上可比较的工具在安全相关属性、代码复杂度和项目特征方面有何差异？”我们发现，可比较的工具可能存在显著差异：安全警报通常仅集中在部分替代方案中，41% 的工具对之间的圈复杂度差异超过 2.5 × \times，而在我们考察的 60% 功能中，某些候选项目仍在活跃维护，而其他项目则已停止维护。

paragraphs.en: RQ4 (Downstream task utility): “Does organizing candidate tools by the taxonomy help agents complete tasks?” We find that taxonomy-guided organization improves task completion on MCP-Atlas ( Bandi et al., 2026 ) for all four evaluated models, with gains of up to 12 points in Pass@0.75 as the candidate set becomes more crowded.
paragraphs.zh: RQ4（下游任务效用）：“按照分类法组织候选工具是否有助于智能体完成任务？”我们发现，在所有四个受评估的模型中，由分类法指导的组织方式都能提升 MCP-Atlas 上的任务完成率（Bandi et al., 2026），随着候选工具集变得更为拥挤，Pass@0.75 的增益最高可达 12 分。

paragraphs.en: In this section, we first introduce the MCP ecosystem and then review prior work in two closely related areas: (1) MCP datasets and benchmarks and (2) software taxonomy construction.
paragraphs.zh: 在本节中，我们首先介绍 MCP 生态系统，然后回顾两个密切相关领域的先前工作：(1) MCP 数据集与基准测试，以及 (2) 软件分类体系构建。

paragraphs.en: MCP protocol, servers, and tools. The Model Context Protocol (MCP), introduced by Anthropic in November 2024, is an open standard for connecting LLM-based applications to external data and functionality ( Anthropic, 2024 ) . An MCP host uses clients to communicate with servers that expose capabilities from external software and services, such as web browsers, IDEs, and databases ( Model Context Protocol, 2026a ) . A server can expose multiple tools. Each tool has a name and JSON input schema and may also provide a natural-language description and output schema ( Model Context Protocol, 2026d ; Model Context Protocol, 2026b ) .
paragraphs.zh: MCP 协议、服务器和工具。 Model Context Protocol（MCP）由 Anthropic 于 2024 年 11 月推出，是一项开放标准，用于将基于 LLM 的应用程序连接到外部数据和功能（Anthropic, 2024）。 MCP 主机通过客户端与服务器通信，这些服务器提供来自外部软件和服务的功能，例如网络浏览器、IDE 和数据库（Model Context Protocol, 2026a）。 一个服务器可以暴露多个工具。 每个工具都有一个名称和 JSON 输入模式，也可以提供自然语言描述和输出模式（Model Context Protocol, 2026d；Model Context Protocol, 2026b）。

paragraphs.zh: 工具发现与选择。 在典型的智能体工作流程中，主机通过 tools/list 获取可用工具的规格信息，并将其提供给 LLM。 根据用户请求和上下文，LLM 利用工具元数据选择工具并生成其参数。 客户端通过 tools/call 调用该工具，其结果会返回给 LLM，用于进一步的推理或操作（Model Context Protocol, 2026a；Model Context Protocol, 2026d）。

paragraphs.en: MCP marketplaces. MCP marketplaces, such as Glama ( Glama, ) and Cline’s MCP Marketplace ( Cline, ) , are discovery platforms operated by companies, communities, or independent maintainers. Server developers can also submit servers, while marketplace operators index listings with descriptions, repository links, and platform-specific categories ( Cline, ; Glama, ) . Users browse or search these catalogs to find servers to install or connect to their agents. However, marketplace organization typically relies on coarse server-level categories, which do not capture fine-grained tool functionality or functional comparability across servers ( Glama, ) . To address this gap, our work constructs a tool-level functional taxonomy to support fine-grained tool discovery and comparison across MCP servers.

paragraphs.en: Ecosystem datasets and measurement. MCPCorpus ( Lin et al., 2025 ) consolidates server and client metadata, while Toeppe et al. ( Toeppe et al., 2026 ) construct a repository dataset with implementation evidence and operational-role labels. Measurement studies examine marketplace growth and overlap ( Guo et al., 2025 ) , security and maintainability ( Hasan et al., 2026 ) , lifecycle threats ( Hou et al., 2026 ) , and registry and server vulnerabilities ( Li and Gao, 2026 ) . paragraphs.en: MCP tool-use and retrieval benchmarks. MCP-Universe ( Luo et al., 2025 ) , MCP-Bench ( Wang et al., 2026b ) , and MCP-Atlas ( Bandi et al., 2026 ) evaluate multi-step tasks using real MCP servers. MCPToolBench++ ( Fan et al., 2025 ) automates task construction, while LiveMCPBench ( Mo et al., 2026 ) emphasizes tool retrieval and composition. Larger resources include MCP-Zero ( Fei et al., 2025 ) , which evaluates on-demand retrieval over 2,797 tools, and MCP-Flow ( Wang et al., 2026a ) , which collects 11,536 tools to generate training and evaluation data. JSPLIT ( Antonioni et al., 2025 ) uses a hierarchical server taxonomy to reduce retrieval and prompt overhead, but its evaluation excludes distractors from the target server’s leaf category. These works focus on tool use for specific tasks within selected servers. paragraphs.en: Software taxonomy construction organizes software artifacts into categories based on shared characteristics, supporting systematic understanding, discovery, and comparison ( Usman et al., 2017 ) . Automated approaches categorize software using semantic analysis, topic modeling, or clustering ( Kawaguchi et al., 2004 ; Tian et al., 2009 ; Altarawy et al., 2018 ) , while other work organizes software domain labels through knowledge bases and human or LLM assistance ( Sas et al., 2023 ; Sas and Capiluppi, 2024 ) . More recently, ATLAS ( Lu et al., 2026 ) constructs hierarchical software repository taxonomies through iterative category design, classification, and refinement, supporting repository retrieval and alternative discovery. MCPacific adapts the iterative taxonomy construction to enable functional characterization and comparison of callable operations across MCP servers.
paragraphs.zh: 软件分类体系构建基于共享特征将软件产物组织到不同类别中，从而支持系统性的理解、发现与比较（Usman 等，2017）。 自动化方法通过语义分析、主题建模或聚类对软件进行分类（Kawaguchi 等，2004；Tian 等，2009；Altarawy 等，2018），而其他研究则通过知识库以及人类或大型语言模型（LLM）的协助来组织软件领域标签（Sas 等，2023；Sas 和 Capiluppi，2024）。 近期，ATLAS（Lu 等，2026）通过迭代的设计、分类与优化类别，构建分层化的软件仓库分类体系，从而支持仓库检索与替代方案发现。 MCPPacific 将迭代分类体系构建方法加以调整，以实现 MCP 服务器间可调用操作的功能特性描述与比较。

paragraphs.en: Figure 1 gives an overview of MCPacific , which proceeds in three phases. First, we collect MCP servers from 17 marketplaces, deduplicate them by repository, and retrieve their source code (§ 3.1 ). Second, we statically analyze the source code to extract tool specifications in a unified five-field schema (§ 3.2 ). Third, we organize the extracted tools into a hierarchical functional taxonomy and assign every tool to it (§ 3.3 ). Each phase builds on the output of the previous one, and the resulting taxonomy serves as the measurement instrument for the analyses in Section 4 .
paragraphs.zh: 图 1 概述了 MCPacific，该流程分为三个阶段。 首先，我们从 17 个市场收集 MCP 服务器，按仓库进行去重，并获取其源代码（§ 3.1）。 其次，我们对源代码进行静态分析，以统一的五字段模式提取工具规范（§ 3.2）。 第三，我们将提取出的工具组织成一个分层功能分类体系，并为每个工具分配相应类别（§ 3.3）。 每个阶段都基于前一阶段的输出，最终形成的分类体系则作为第 4 节中分析所使用的测量工具。

paragraphs.en: To achieve broad coverage of publicly available MCP servers, we construct an initial pool of marketplaces and directories from prior MCP ecosystem studies ( Guo et al., 2025 ; Chen et al., 2026 ; Lin et al., 2025 ) , supplemented by community-maintained resource collections and public discussions. After consolidating duplicate or overlapping sources, we retain 17 distinct MCP marketplaces.

paragraphs.en: To collect data from these marketplaces, we develop an automated collection pipeline with four stages: (i) entry collection, (ii) repository validation, (iii) repository deduplication, and (iv) source-code retrieval. Because MCP marketplaces expose heterogeneous interfaces and page structures, we implement source-specific collectors to enumerate server entries through public APIs, SDKs, web pages, or structured data embedded in those pages. We then normalize project names, descriptions, source-provided categories and tags, repository links, and provenance metadata into a unified JSONL schema, producing the raw collection . Next, we validate associated repositories using the GitHub REST API, excluding inaccessible or empty repositories and documentation-only projects without executable source code. For the remaining entries, we resolve repository URLs to canonical repository identifiers and deduplicate records that refer to the same repository. Finally, we retrieve the source code of each unique repository for subsequent source-level analysis.
paragraphs.zh: 为了从这些市场平台收集数据，我们开发了一个包含四个阶段的自动化收集流程：(i) 条目收集、(ii) 仓库验证、(iii) 仓库去重以及 (iv) 源代码获取。 由于 MCP 市场平台提供了异构的接口和页面结构，我们为不同来源实现了专门的收集器，通过公共 API、SDK、网页或嵌入在这些页面中的结构化数据来枚举服务器条目。 接着，我们将项目名称、描述、来源提供的分类和标签、仓库链接以及来源元数据标准化为统一的 JSONL 格式，从而生成原始收集数据。 接下来，我们使用 GitHub REST API 验证相关的仓库，排除无法访问或空的仓库，以及没有可执行源代码的纯文档项目。 对于剩余的条目，我们将仓库 URL 解析为标准仓库标识符，并去除指向同一仓库的重叠记录。 最后，我们为每个唯一的仓库获取源代码，以便进行后续的源代码级分析。

paragraphs.en: To support functional taxonomy construction, we extract tool descriptions and function signatures from MCP server source code. This is challenging because MCP tools are implemented differently across programming languages, SDKs, and frameworks. As illustrated in Figure 2 , tools may be defined through decorators or annotations, explicit registration calls, tool objects or builders, wrappers or factories, or low-level protocol handlers. Moreover, tool metadata and execution logic may reside in different parts of the codebase. We therefore develop a cross-language static analysis pipeline that recognizes diverse tool declaration patterns and resolves them to their corresponding implementation functions.
paragraphs.zh: 为了支持功能分类体系的构建，我们从 MCP 服务器源代码中提取工具描述和功能签名。 这一过程充满挑战，因为 MCP 工具在不同编程语言、SDK 和框架中的实现方式各不相同。 如图 2 所示，工具可能通过装饰器或注解、显式注册调用、工具对象或构建器、包装器或工厂，或者底层协议处理程序来定义。 此外，工具元数据和执行逻辑可能位于代码库的不同部分。 因此，我们开发了一条跨语言静态分析流程，能够识别多种工具声明模式，并将其解析为对应的实现函数。

paragraphs.en: (i) Language scope and pattern identification. We first analyze the distribution of primary implementation languages across all 124,267 source-available server projects in our collection. We then select the seven most prevalent languages for tool extraction: Python, TypeScript, JavaScript, Go, Rust, Java, and C#. In total, these languages cover 110,482 repositories (88.9%). For each selected language, we manually inspect tool implementations and iteratively identify tool declaration and registration patterns. This analysis yields 56 patterns spanning decorators and annotations, explicit registration calls, tool objects and builders, wrappers and factories, and low-level protocol handlers.

paragraphs.en: (ii) Tool recognition and entry-function localization. We develop language-specific static analyzers that recognize these patterns in abstract syntax trees (ASTs) ( Falleri and Martinez, 2024 ; Sun et al., 2023 ; Dyer et al., 2014 ) . For each recognized tool declaration or registration, the analyzers recover its metadata and resolve the associated handler, callback, or method reference to an entry function that implements the tool’s execution logic. For low-level protocol implementations, the analyzers link tool declarations to invocation-dispatch logic and follow branches selected by tool name to locate the corresponding entry functions. We also analyze the registration patterns, AST backends, and entry-function resolution rules. This unified representation provides a consistent schema for subsequent functional classification and comparison.

paragraphs.en: Given the eligible tool set 𝒯 \mathcal{T} , we aim to construct a rooted functional taxonomy 𝒢 \mathcal{G} and assign each tool to exactly one leaf. Each internal node v v partitions its tool set T v T_{v} along a single splitting dimension δ v \delta_{v} , i.e., the functional property that distinguishes its children, such as the target service, the resource, or the operation. Each child category is defined by a name, a description, and explicit inclusion and exclusion criteria. Partitioning continues until each leaf groups functionally comparable tools: tools that accomplish the same primary user-level task under comparable inputs and conditions and can therefore substitute for one another. For example, execute_sql , run_sql , and execute_query belong to the same leaf if each executes a user-provided SQL query against a database, despite differences in naming or implementation.

paragraphs.en: The core decision at each node is which dimension to split on and how to define categories so that every tool fits exactly one. Neither embedding clustering nor an LLM alone makes this decision well. Clustering groups similar tools but cannot name the dimension that separates the groups; an LLM can propose meaningful dimensions but may not fit the tools that actually exist. We therefore let an LLM propose each node’s design from sampled tools and test it on other sampled tools, guided by three design goals. (R1) Categories describe what a tool does, independent of the server or marketplace that lists it. (R2) Every category design is tested on real tools before it is used. (R3) The procedure scales to over a million tools, so per-tool LLM calls are the exception rather than the rule.
paragraphs.zh: 每个节点的核心决策是选择哪个维度进行划分，以及如何定义类别，以确保每个工具都恰好属于一个类别。 单独使用嵌入聚类或大型语言模型都无法很好地做出这一决策。 聚类可以将相似的工具分组，但无法指出区分这些组的维度；而大型语言模型虽然能提出有意义的维度，却可能无法匹配实际存在的工具。 因此，我们让大型语言模型根据采样工具提出每个节点的设计方案，并通过其他采样工具进行验证，整个过程由三个设计目标指导。 (R1) 类别应描述工具的功能，而不受列出该工具的服务器或市场平台的影响。 (R2) 每个类别设计在投入使用前，都必须通过真实工具的测试。 (R3) 该流程可扩展至超过一百万个工具，因此针对单个工具调用大型语言模型属于例外情况，而非常规操作。

paragraphs.en: The functional taxonomy construction proceeds in five stages. paragraphs.en: Leaf test (line 3 – 4 ) . A singleton node is immediately accepted as a leaf. paragraphs.en: Sampling (lines 5 ) . Category design and pilot validation use disjoint samples. paragraphs.en: ➍ Full corpus mapping. Development tools keep their construction assignments. Every other eligible tool is first matched against embeddings of complete root-to-leaf paths (the names and definitions along each path), using Eq. 1 with separately calibrated thresholds. If this match is not decisive, the tool is routed top-down by ➌, with the Classifier deciding at the node where Eq. 1 fails. A leaf that looked homogeneous on a few development tools may receive many diverse corpus tools, after full-corpus mapping, unresolved and low-confidence tools are collected for post-classification refinement and human review. Finally, because each node chooses its dimension locally, different branches reach the same level of specificity at different depths. An LLM therefore reviews a sample of root-to-leaf dimension sequences and derives an ordered set of semantic ranks ; each dimension receives the rank it holds in most paths that contain it. This level alignment only labels nodes and leaves all memberships unchanged; cross-domain comparisons in RQ1 use ranks instead of raw depth.

paragraphs.en: ➎ Human refinement. The residual set U U contains the tools that the Classifier could not place, or placed with low confidence, during construction or corpus mapping. Even a small residual fraction of a million tools is too large to label exhaustively, so we resolve U U in rounds. In each round, reviewers label 200 tools sampled from U U across the nodes at which they failed: each tool is assigned to an existing category, marked as a capability missing under that node, or marked as not a functional tool. We use these labels in two ways: (i) we add rules and labeled examples to the Classifier’s instructions for the affected nodes, and (ii) when several tools share a missing capability, we add a new leaf category, which must pass the same checks as any design (category design and node finalization). paragraphs.en: Our analyses rely on two properties of the taxonomy: tools are placed in the correct leaf, and tools that share a leaf are functionally comparable. We evaluate both on a uniform random sample of 200 tools with a leaf assignment. For each sampled tool, we ask (i) whether it belongs to its assigned leaf ( assignment precision ), and (ii) whether it is functionally comparable to a randomly chosen tool from the same leaf ( leaf comparability ); We use an LLM judge (gpt-5.6-terra), a different model than the models used for construction, to answer both questions given the tools’ specifications, the root-to-leaf path with its category definitions, and our definition of functional comparability. To validate the judge, two authors independently labeled a random subset of 100 tools without seeing the judge’s answers and resolved disagreements by discussion.
paragraphs.zh: 我们的分析依赖于该分类体系的两个特性：工具被置于正确的叶节点，且共享同一叶节点的工具在功能上具有可比性。 我们对这两项特性均基于一个包含 200 个已分配叶节点的工具的均匀随机样本进行评估。 对于每个被采样的工具，我们提出两个问题：(i) 它是否属于其被分配的叶节点（分配精确度），以及 (ii) 它与从同一叶节点中随机选取的工具在功能上是否具有可比性（叶节点可比性）；我们使用一个 LLM 判官（gpt-5.6-terra）——该模型不同于构建过程中使用的模型——根据工具规格、从根节点到叶节点的路径及其类别定义，以及我们对功能可比性的定义，来回答这两个问题。 为了验证该判官的可靠性，两位作者在不查看判官答案的情况下，独立地对 100 个工具的随机子集进行了标注，并通过讨论解决了分歧。

paragraphs.en: Prior MCP studies characterize the ecosystem at the server level, mostly through marketplace-defined categories ( Guo et al., 2025 ; Lin et al., 2025 ) . Server-level labels, however, cannot reveal which operations agents can actually invoke, how many distinct tool capabilities exist, or how finely these capabilities must be distinguished. Using the taxonomy as a measurement instrument, RQ1 examines which domains MCP tools serve (Finding 1), whether large domains also offer more diverse capabilities (Finding 2), and how deep the taxonomy must go before tools in a domain become functionally comparable. The analysis covers the 953,172 tools assigned to one of 58,915 leaf capabilities.
paragraphs.zh: 早期的 MCP 研究主要从服务器层面描述生态系统，通常通过市场定义的分类进行（Guo 等，2025；Lin 等，2025）。 然而，服务器层面的标签无法揭示智能体实际可以调用哪些操作、存在多少种不同的工具能力，或这些能力需要被区分到何种精细程度。 RQ1 将这一分类体系作为测量工具，旨在探究 MCP 工具服务于哪些领域（发现 1）、大型领域是否也提供更丰富的能力（发现 2），以及分类体系需要细化到何种深度，才能使同一领域内的工具在功能上具有可比性。 该分析涵盖了被分配至 58,915 个叶级能力中的 953,172 个工具。

paragraphs.en: Finding 1: MCP has outgrown software development: 85% of tools serve other domains. Figure 3 shows that Software Development is the largest individual domain with 143,202 tools (15.0%), followed by Infrastructure (11.3%) and Business (11.0%). The remaining of tools span domains including Finance, Media, Communication, Healthcare, and Education. These results show that MCP is no longer primarily a developer-tool ecosystem; it has become a general-purpose integration layer covering a wide range of application domains. Consequently, prior benchmarks built from a few dozen curated servers ( Wang et al., 2026b ; Bandi et al., 2026 ; Luo et al., 2025 ) therefore cover only a small part of the functional range that deployed agents face.
paragraphs.zh: 发现 1：MCP 已超越软件开发领域：85% 的工具服务于其他领域。 图 3 显示，软件开发是单个领域中最大的类别，包含 143,202 个工具（占 15.0%），其次是基础设施（11.3%）和商业（11.0%）。 其余工具覆盖的领域包括金融、媒体、通信、医疗保健和教育。 这些结果表明，MCP 不再主要是一个开发者工具生态系统；它已成为一个通用集成层，涵盖广泛的应用领域。 因此，基于少数几十台精选服务器构建的先前基准（Wang et al., 2026b; Bandi et al., 2026; Luo et al., 2025）仅覆盖了部署的智能体所面临的功能范围的很小一部分。

paragraphs.en: Finding 2: More tools do not mean more capabilities: large domains fragment, while smaller domains often repeat the same capabilities. A domain can be large for two different reasons: it offers many distinct capabilities (leaf categories of functionally comparable tools), or many tools implement the same few capabilities. Because these cases pose different problems for users when retrieving tools, we ask whether tool volume reflects capability breadth or redundancy.
paragraphs.zh: 发现 2：更多工具并不意味着更强的能力：大型领域会碎片化，而小型领域往往重复相同的能力。 一个领域可能因两种不同原因而变得庞大：它提供了许多不同的能力（功能上可比较的工具的叶类别），或者许多工具实现了相同的少数几种能力。 由于这些情况在用户检索工具时提出了不同的问题，我们想知道工具的数量是反映了能力的广度还是重复性。

paragraphs.en: For each domain, we count its capabilities and measure the share of its tools in its largest and five largest capabilities (Table 4 ). Software Development spans 8,213 capabilities, yet its largest one holds only 0.8% of its tools and its five largest 3.3%; Business is similarly dispersed (0.8% and 3.4%). In contrast, Mathematics has only 154 capabilities, and its five largest hold 34.6% of its tools; Tooling shows the same pattern (295 capabilities; 22.7%). Tool volume thus reflects breadth in some domains and redundancy in others, which creates two distinct challenges. In fragmented domains, the challenge is discovery : users must locate one of thousands of narrow capabilities, which coarse server-level categories cannot support. In concentrated domains, the challenge is selection among many tools that implement the same capability, which we examine in RQ2 and RQ4.

paragraphs.en: For each domain, we measure leaf depth, i.e., the number of splits from the root, and the share of tools at depth 8 or deeper (Figure 4 ). These long tails suggest that the deep domains combine many providers, resources, and operation variants, so some of their capabilities are identified only after many successive distinctions. paragraphs.en: Answer to RQ1: The MCP ecosystem is functionally broad with 18 domains and 58,915 distinct capabilities. Yet this breadth is uneven: a few general-purpose domains dominate tool volume; Large domains span many narrow capabilities, whereas some smaller domains concentrate on a few. Users need a tool-level map with domain-adaptive depth to discover capabilities and choose among functionally comparable tools.

paragraphs.en: When a tool is unavailable, deprecated, or insecure, an agent can only recover if another tool performs the same operation. Conversely, if many developers implement the same capabilities while others remain uncovered, effort is duplicated, and parts of the ecosystem are fragile. RQ2 uses leaf co-membership as a proxy for functional comparability and examines how many alternative tools have (Finding 4) and how tool supply is distributed across capabilities (Finding 5).

paragraphs.en: Finding 4: Alternatives are the norm: 98.5% of tools have at least one functionally comparable alternative, and 74.1% have at least 20. To assess whether agents and users can routinely choose among tools with comparable capabilities, we count, for each tool, its candidate alternatives, i.e., the other tools in the same taxonomy leaf, and report the share of tools with none, at least one, and at least 20 alternatives, overall and per domain (lines in Figure 3 ). Only 1.53% of tools have no alternative, whereas 98.47% have at least one and 74.14% have at least 20. The share with at least one alternative is high in every domain; domains differ mainly in how many alternatives tools have: Mathematics, Tooling, and Web have the highest shares of tools with at least 20 alternatives, whereas fewer than half of the tools in Education and Other do. For most tools, the open question is therefore not whether an alternative exists but which one to choose, which motivates comparing how alternatives differ (RQ3) and organizing retrieval around comparable candidates (RQ4).
paragraphs.zh: 发现 4：替代方案是常态：98.5% 的工具至少有一个功能相当的替代方案，74.1% 的工具至少有 20 个。 为了评估智能体和用户是否能够常规地在能力相当的工具中进行选择，我们对每个工具统计其候选替代方案的数量，即同一分类法叶节点中的其他工具，并报告完全没有替代方案、至少有一个以及至少 20 个替代方案的工具比例（总体及各领域），如图中第 3 行的数据所示。 仅有 1.53% 的工具没有替代方案，而 98.47% 的工具至少有一个，74.14% 的工具至少有 20 个。 每个领域中至少有 1 个替代方案的比例都很高；各领域的差异主要体现在工具所具有的替代方案数量上：数学、工具和 Web 领域拥有至少 20 个替代方案的工具比例最高，而教育和其他领域的此类工具比例则不足一半。 因此，对于大多数工具而言，开放性问题不在于是否存在替代方案，而在于应选择哪一个，这促使我们比较替代方案之间的差异（研究问题 3），并围绕可比较的候选方案组织检索（研究问题 4）。

paragraphs.en: Finding 5: Nearly one quarter of observed capabilities have no alternative. Although alternatives are common among tools (Finding 4), 58,915 capabilities (24.80%) contain exactly one observed tool. We call these single-tool capabilities . To understand the support behind their sole implementations, we examine their domain distribution and the characteristics of their supporting repositories. Single-tool capabilities are most prevalent in Other and Infrastructure, representing 42.16% and 35.40% of capabilities within these domains, respectively. Examples include Cryptographic Proofs and Pronunciation Dictionary Management. Since agents have no fallback for these capabilities, we examine whether their sole implementations are well supported. We compare repositories that support at least one single-tool capability with repositories whose capabilities all have alternatives, counting each repository once, in terms of GitHub stars, recent activity (a push within 90 days before collection), and owner type. Repositories supporting single-tool capabilities are more often recently active (47.50% versus 39.26%) and organization-owned (18.83% versus 14.61%), differences of 8.24 and 4.22 percentage points, respectively. Their median star count is slightly higher (2 versus 1). Thus, lacking alternatives does not imply weak repository support. Single-tool capabilities are, in fact, backed by more recently active repositories on average. One possible explanation is that some tools serve specialized organizational needs, motivating continued development without attracting alternative implementations.

paragraphs.en: RQ2 shows that most tools have functionally comparable alternatives, so users and agents routinely face a choice among them. paragraphs.en: To examine differences within groups, we select ten groups that together cover all security categories (79 tools; Figure 6 ). Every group contains both security alerted and alert-free tools, and security alerted tools make up 11.1–40.0% of each group; Alerted tools in the same group also differ in the kind of risk they carry: in all nine groups with more than one alerted tool, the alerts span at least two security categories. In Versioned commit , for example, one tool sends unencrypted HTTP requests (transport security), while another builds regular expressions dynamically, a potential denial-of-service risk (resource management); in CORS misconfiguration , one alerted tool lacks input validation and another lacks access control. Input validation is the most widespread concern, appearing in nine of the ten groups, and four tools combine it with a second category, such as authentication in Analysis or credential exposure in Project scope . Even when alerted tools share a category, the underlying issues can differ: in Chromatin accessibility profiling , three tools are flagged for input validation, but two pass unchecked input to subprocess calls, whereas the third builds URLs dynamically. Functional similarity therefore does not imply similar security posture: in every examined group, users could choose an alert-free tool with the same functionality, and the alerts of the others point to distinct, rule-specific risks.

The analysis covers 86,387 pairs among 55,651 tools in 16,484 leaf–language units (Figure 6 ). Identical implementations are uncommon: only 23.64% of pairs have the same CCN and 9.19% the same NLOC. paragraphs.en: Beyond the code itself, users weigh project-level signals such as recent activity and ownership when choosing a tool; we therefore ask whether these signals also vary among functionally comparable alternatives.

paragraphs.en: We analyze the 21,070 groups whose tools come from at least two repositories with available metadata (97,279 tools from 29,772 repositories across all 18 domains), counting each repository once per group. For five repository attributes, namely recent activity (not archived and pushed within 180 days of collection), owner type (user or organization), primary language, archived status, and fork status, we compute the share of repository pairs within a group that disagree, D g , a = ( m g , a 2 ) − 1 ∑ i < j 𝟏 [ x i , a ≠ x j , a ] D_{g,a}=\binom{m_{g,a}}{2}^{-1}\sum_{i<j}\mathbf{1}[x_{i,a}\neq x_{j,a}] , where m g , a ≥ 2 m_{g,a}\geq 2 is the number of repositories in group g g with an observed value x i , a x_{i,a} of attribute a a , and average it with equal weight across groups to obtain D ¯ a \bar{D}_{a} (Figure 8 ). Candidate projects differ most in primary language ( D ¯ = 49.87 % \bar{D}=49.87\% ), recent activity (35.31%), and owner type (31.36%); in 60.38% of groups, at least one candidate project is recently active and another is not. Archived status (2.36%) and fork status (0.91%) rarely differ, likely because few repositories are archived or forked in the first place. paragraphs.en: Evaluation Setup. We evaluate MCPacific on the same 100 released tasks from MCP-Atlas ( Bandi et al., 2026 ) , which contain multi-tool instructions and expert-annotated reference trajectories. We map all 220 unique benchmark tools to the MCPacific database and taxonomy. For each task, the flat list (baseline) and hierarchical taxonomy ( MCPacific ) receive exactly the same enabled tools and differ only in how those tools are organized and retrieved.
paragraphs.zh: 评估设置。 我们在 MCP-Atlas（Bandi et al., 2026）发布的相同 100 个任务上对 MCPacific 进行评估，这些任务包含多工具指令和专家标注的参考轨迹。 我们将所有 220 种独特的基准测试工具映射到 MCPacific 数据库和分类体系中。 对于每个任务，扁平列表（基线）和分层分类体系（MCPacific）都获得完全相同的可用工具，二者的唯一区别在于这些工具的组织和检索方式。

paragraphs.en: In the baseline, the model receives the complete flat list of enabled tools. In MCPacific , the same tools are organized into a task-specific subtree extracted from the global functional taxonomy. Starting at the root, the model retains clearly or potentially relevant branches and expands only those branches. It then selects a complete tool plan from the tools reached through the retained paths. Thus, MCPacific uses the taxonomy for retrieval but does not change the tools available to the model.

paragraphs.en: We evaluate GPT-5.6-Luna , GPT-5.6-Terra , GPT-5.5 , and GPT-5.4 under both conditions, holding task prompts and reasoning-effort settings fixed. Following MCP-Atlas, we report two complementary metrics. Mean Claim Coverage measures how fully task requirements are satisfied: each reference claim receives 1, 0.5, or 0 for full, partial, or no fulfillment, respectively, with scores averaged first within each task and then across tasks. Pass@0.75 measures the proportion of tasks achieving at least 75% claim coverage. The former captures average coverage, including partial progress, while the latter captures how often a specified coverage target is reached. We use GPT-5.4 to judge claim fulfillment with a fixed prompt and scoring rubric.
paragraphs.zh: 我们在两种条件下对 GPT-5.6-Luna、GPT-5.6-Terra、GPT-5.5 和 GPT-5.4 进行了评估，同时保持任务提示和推理努力设置不变。 遵循 MCP-Atlas 的做法，我们报告了两个互补的指标。 平均声明覆盖度衡量任务要求得到满足的程度：每个参考声明分别获得 1、0.5 或 0 分，表示完全满足、部分满足或未满足，然后先在各任务内对分数求平均，再跨任务求平均。 Pass@0.75 衡量至少达到 75% 声明覆盖度的任务比例。 前者反映平均覆盖度（包括部分进展），而后者反映达到指定覆盖度目标的情况频率。 我们使用 GPT-5.4，通过固定的提示和评分标准来判断声明的满足情况。

paragraphs.en: Finding 9: Taxonomy-guided retrieval improves task performance across all four models without adding tools. As shown in the first section of Table 6 , MCPacific outperforms the flat-list baseline on both metrics for all four models. Mean Claim Coverage increases by 0.69 to 4.43 percentage points, while Pass@0.75 increases by 1 to 9 points. GPT-5.5 obtains the largest coverage gain, increasing from 74.22% to 78.66%, whereas GPT-5.6-Luna obtains the largest Pass@0.75 gain, increasing from 61.00% to 70.00%. The consistency of these improvements indicates that MCPacific ’s benefit is not tied to a particular model. Organizing candidates by functional capability helps the model focus on task-relevant regions of the tool space and retrieve evidence supporting more reference claims. A small average coverage gain can produce a large Pass@0.75 increase when several tasks move from slightly below to slightly above the 0.75 threshold.

paragraphs.en: Finding 10: MCPacific is more robust when the candidate-tool space becomes crowded. To test the efficiency to a broader tool scope, we use GPT-5.6-Luna and augment each task’s original enabled-tool set with 30 and 50 additional random tools. The original candidate sets contain an average of 15.37 tools per task, with a minimum of 7 and a maximum of 30. The second section of Table 1 shows that MCPacific improves Mean Claim Coverage by 2.73 points and Pass@0.75 by 9 points on the original candidate sets. With 30 additional tools, the two methods perform similarly. However, with 50 additional tools, the difference becomes substantially larger. MCPacific improves Mean Claim Coverage from 70.01% to 74.46% and Pass@0.75 from 54.00% to 66.00%, corresponding to gains of 4.45 and 12 points, respectively. These results indicate that hierarchical organization becomes more useful when the flat candidate list contains more tools and broader tool scope. The baseline must consider every tool in a single selection context, whereas MCPacific can discard unrelated functional branches before final tool selection. Its advantage is more obvious in the larger candidate-set condition, where flat-list retrieval experiences the greatest degradation.

paragraphs.en: Internal validity. The main internal threat is error in our automated pipeline. Static extraction may miss dynamically registered tools or resolve entry functions incorrectly. We mitigate this by deriving 30 recognition patterns through manual inspection of implementations in all seven languages and excluding tools with missing or unreadable descriptions. LLMs may also misclassify tools or behave non-deterministically. We mitigate this by evaluating each category design on a separate pilot sample, checking each node for mutually exclusive and exhaustive categories, sending unresolved cases to human review, and validating final assignments with an LLM judge calibrated against two human annotators (Section 3.3.4 ). Semgrep ( Semgrep, Inc., 2026 ) rules can produce false positives and negatives, and an LLM further maps alerts to categories. We therefore interpret these alerts as potential, rather than confirmed, issues and report the corresponding rule-level evidence. Finally, in RQ4, GPT-5.4 serves both as an evaluated model and as the judge. Because the same judge, prompt, and rubric are applied to both the baseline and MCPacific , our analysis focuses on their relative differences rather than absolute scores.
paragraphs.zh: 内部效度。 主要的内部威胁来自我们自动化流程中的错误。 静态提取可能会遗漏动态注册的工具，或错误解析入口函数。 我们通过手动检查全部七种语言中的实现，推导出 30 种识别模式，并排除描述缺失或无法阅读的工具，从而缓解这一问题。 LLM 也可能对工具进行分类错误，或表现出非确定性行为。 我们通过为每个类别设计在独立的试点样本上进行评估、检查每个节点是否满足互斥且完备的类别要求、将未解决案例提交给人工审核，并使用经过两名人类标注者校准的 LLM 裁判验证最终分配结果（第 3.3.4 节），来缓解这一问题。 Semgrep（Semgrep, Inc., 2026）规则可能产生假阳性或假阴性结果，而 LLM 还会进一步将警报映射到相应类别。 因此，我们将这些警报解释为潜在问题而非已确认的问题，并报告相应的规则级证据。 最后，在 RQ4 中，GPT-5.4 既作为被评估模型，也作为裁判。 由于基准模型和 MCPacific 都使用了相同的裁判、提示词和评分标准，我们的分析重点在于它们之间的相对差异，而非绝对分数。

paragraphs.en: External validity. Our dataset covers 17 marketplaces but includes only source-available servers written in the seven most common languages, which account for 88.9% of collected repositories; closed-source and remote-only servers are outside our scope. The taxonomy is initially constructed from 5,000 servers and may therefore miss rare capabilities, although full-corpus mapping, leaf re-expansion, and human refinement extend its coverage. Because the MCP ecosystem evolves rapidly, our findings represent a snapshot at collection time. However, the automated collection, extraction, and mapping pipeline enables the analysis to be repeated on future snapshots.

paragraphs.en: Its central lesson is that the open tool ecosystem is best understood through what tools do, not where they are listed: viewed functionally, the ecosystem offers abundant but uneven alternatives whose differences matter, and this structure is directly usable by agents. For platform and agent developers, this suggests organizing tools by function to make discovery and fallback tractable at scale; for users, it means that choosing among functionally comparable tools requires security, code, and maintenance signals that marketplaces do not yet provide. In future work, we plan to track the ecosystem across snapshots, verify substitutability between comparable tools at the schema and behavior level, and integrate MCPacific into agent frameworks for open-world tool selection.
paragraphs.zh: 其核心观点是：开放工具生态系统的最佳理解方式应着眼于工具的功能，而非其列出的位置；从功能角度而言，该生态系统提供了丰富但分布不均的替代方案，这些差异具有重要意义，且这一结构可直接被智能体使用。 对于平台和智能体开发者而言，这意味着应按功能对工具进行组织，以便在大规模场景下实现便捷的发现与备用方案切换；对于用户而言，则意味着在功能上可比较的工具之间做出选择时，需要依赖市场平台尚未提供的安全性、代码质量和维护状态等信号。 在未来的工作中，我们计划通过不同时间点的快照追踪该生态系统的发展，在模式和行为层面验证可比较工具之间的可替代性，并将 MCPacific 集成到智能体框架中，以实现开放世界中的工具选择。

paragraphs.en: Our study analyzes publicly available MCP marketplaces, repository metadata, and tool specifications. We do not collect private user interactions, credentials, or other intentionally non-public data, and we report aggregate results rather than evaluating individuals. Nevertheless, consolidating tools into a searchable taxonomy may increase the discoverability of capabilities that could be misused, while automated classification may reproduce marketplace biases or incorrectly characterize particular tools. Thus, we expose category definitions and validation results, and treat assignments as analytical annotations rather than security or quality endorsements. We will release only the information necessary for reproducibility, and recommend that downstream users independently examine a tool’s provenance, permissions, maintenance, and security before deployment.
paragraphs.zh: 我们的研究分析了公开可用的 MCP 市场、仓库元数据和工具规范。 我们不收集用户的私人互动、凭证或其他有意不公开的数据，并且我们报告的是汇总结果，而非对个体进行评估。 然而，将工具整合到可搜索的分类体系中，可能会增加那些可能被滥用的功能的可发现性；而自动分类则可能重复市场中的偏见，或对特定工具做出错误描述。 因此，我们公开了类别定义和验证结果，并将这些分类视为分析性注释，而非安全性或质量的认可。 我们将仅发布确保可重复性所必需的信息，并建议下游用户在部署前独立审查工具的来源、权限、维护状况和安全性。
